nodes.label: Lift drill into superpowers as evals/ — design spec
evals/ as the canonical LLM-behavior eval harness
nodes.rationale: Drill (obra/drill) was already the de facto eval harness — PRI-1397 had lifted ~22 superpowers bash tests into drill scenarios and a recent superpowers commit removed a redundant bash test 'replaced by drill behavioral coverage'; this spec completes the migration by making evals/ the canonical home, with a meaningful documented split between tests/ (plugin infrastructure) and evals/ (LLM actor+verifier behavior).

nodes.label: Per-bash-test deletion gate: verifiable drill coverage of every assertion
nodes.rationale: A bash test is deleted only if a drill scenario verifiably covers every assertion it makes (per-assertion table produced by an independent subagent); if any check is unmatched the default is to keep the bash test or extend the scenario, so no coverage is silently lost.

nodes.label: Subagent-gated verification protocol for the migration
nodes.rationale: Every change category (deletions, verbatim copy with per-file SHA-256 checksums, path-default change, stale-reference scrub, final adversarial review) is cross-checked by an independent subagent before commit, and each subagent's output is summarized in the commit message so the trail is auditable.

nodes.label: Drill: Python skill-compliance benchmark (tmux sessions, LLM actor + verifier)
nodes.rationale: Named external tool being migrated: drives real tmux sessions, runs an LLM actor as simulated user, an LLM verifier on the transcript, reports pass/fail per scenario; supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Copilot CLI. The Python package keeps its drill name inside evals/ to keep the diff small.
